questions.q: What is the main lesson of Anscombe's quartet?
options: Datasets with identical summary statistics can look completely different when plotted
Correlation always equals 0.82 for small datasets
Outliers can be safely ignored in small datasets
Scatter plots are the only chart worth using
questions.explain: All four sets share the same means, spread and correlation, yet their plots show a line, a curve, an outlier and a single extreme point.

questions.q: Why do summary statistics alone often mislead?
options: They are usually calculated incorrectly by pandas
They compress a dataset into a few numbers and discard its shape
They only work on categorical data
They cannot be calculated on more than ten rows
questions.explain: Means, standard deviations and correlations describe a dataset in a few numbers; curves, clusters and outliers disappear in that compression.

questions.q: In Anscombe's Set II, what does the plot reveal that the correlation of 0.82 hides?
options: A single extreme point creating the correlation
The data is a smooth curve, so a straight line is the wrong model
There are missing values in the x column
The data is random noise
questions.explain: Set II follows a clean curve. A fitted straight line and a 0.82 correlation make it look linear when it is not.

A chart published in an annual report
A chart that has been fully styled with brand colors
A quick, rough chart made for yourself to find surprises and check assumptions
questions.explain: Exploratory charts are for the analyst: fast, unpolished and numerous. Explanatory charts are for the audience.

questions.q: Which habit does this lesson recommend before trusting a summary of your data?
options: Calculate a second summary statistic
Delete the outliers
Plot the data
Sort the DataFrame
questions.explain: Always look at the data. A plot exposes shape, outliers and nonlinearity that summary numbers hide.
